title: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus

cards.name: Fixed 60 Hz simulation step with clamped delta
cards.summary: The engine advances game time from a hardware tick counter, clamps each update to one or two frame periods and applies a global time scale.
cards.behavior: Each update reads the processor tick counter, converts the elapsed ticks to seconds and clamps the result between one and two 1/60 s frame periods. The clamped delta is multiplied by a global rate and a power-up rate, so slow-motion abilities stretch object motion without changing how often the world updates. If the scaled delta is at least one frame period, it also becomes the real delta used for effects that must stay in sync with slowed gameplay.

constants.name: Fixed simulation frame rate
constants.unit: frames per second of simulation time, advanced on every engine update at 60 Hz

constants.name: Maximum delta clamp
constants.unit: frame periods per update at 60 Hz, giving an upper bound of 1/30 s

constants.name: Processor tick rate
constants.unit: hardware ticks per second of real time, converted on every 60 Hz update

constants.name: Default global time scale
constants.unit: dimensionless time multiplier, applied on every 60 Hz update

cards.name: Analog stick calibration and play-input gating
cards.summary: Four analog channels use symmetric deflection limits, while menu and cutscene modes suppress gameplay input.
cards.behavior: When a pad becomes ready, the engine clears its button state and installs symmetric lower and upper deflection limits on four analog channels. Those calibrated ranges feed the movement axes used by the player controller. A separate input mode narrows what reaches gameplay: normal play gets the full pad, menu and hands-off cutscene states replace it with reduced mappings, and an unclassified state maps to mode zero.

constants.name: Upper analog deflection bound
constants.unit: normalized stick deflection, sampled once per input poll in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Lower analog deflection bound
constants.unit: normalized stick deflection, sampled once per input poll in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Calibrated analog channels
constants.unit: axis channels per pad, calibrated once when the pad reports ready in the 60 Hz loop

cards.name: Scoped camera zoom policy
cards.summary: The camera keeps a small stack of look modes; the scoped mode clamps field of view to a ten-to-one range and pulls the near clip in tight.
cards.behavior: A camera look policy keeps a small stack of look modes and pushes or pops them as the player changes view. Activating the scoped look records the current pan and tilt, resets zoom velocity, and constrains field of view between the full base field and one tenth of it. The near clip is pulled in to 49 world units so the focused character does not intersect the view, and the previous near clip is stored for restoration. A reticle screen fraction of 0.5 and an unset radius of -1 describe the default sniper framing.

constants.name: Maximum zoom factor
constants.unit: field-of-view divisor, applied once when the scoped look activates; camera then updates at 60 Hz

constants.name: Look-mode stack depth
constants.unit: stack entries, pushed or popped per camera event in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Scoped near clip
constants.unit: world units, applied once when the scoped look activates and held per 60 Hz update

constants.name: Default sniper screen fraction
constants.unit: fraction of screen radius, evaluated per camera update at 60 Hz

constants.name: Unset sniper radius
constants.unit: world units sentinel meaning no radius override, set once at camera init in the 60 Hz loop

cards.name: Binocular scouting view
cards.summary: The binocular view is a fixed 4:3 style scouting lens with a centred reticle, smooth normalized zoom and a compass-bar offset.
cards.behavior: While the player sweeps the binocular view across a level, the scouting lens uses a fixed overlay with its reticle at the centre of that rectangle. Zoom input is scaled by one percent per unit and clamped between full zoom-out and full zoom-in, so a small stick change produces a smooth optical pull rather than a snap. Resetting the view returns the reticle to centre and sets the compass bar to its default screen offset, keeping the 3D aim point readable.

constants.name: Overlay width
constants.unit: pixels of the binocular overlay, set once when the blot is created in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Overlay height
constants.unit: pixels of the binocular overlay, set once when the blot is created in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Compass bar offset
constants.unit: normalized screen fraction, set once when the view resets in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Zoom input scale
constants.unit: normalized zoom fraction per input unit, applied per 60 Hz update

constants.name: Reticle horizontal centre
constants.unit: pixels from overlay origin, evaluated on every draw at 60 Hz

constants.name: Reticle vertical centre
constants.unit: pixels from overlay origin, evaluated on every draw at 60 Hz

cards.name: Guard vision envelope
cards.summary: Guard sight combines a hard range, a vertical tolerance and a cone that widens near the guard and narrows with distance.
cards.behavior: A guard rejects a target whose height differs by more than the vertical tolerance, then rejects it beyond the maximum horizontal sense range. Inside that range the permitted view angle depends on distance: full pi radians at the inner radius, tapering linearly toward a quarter pi by the outer radius. A successful check latches the guard as having detected the target until the check fails again.

constants.name: Inner detection radius
constants.unit: world units, evaluated per AI update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Outer detection radius
constants.unit: world units, evaluated per AI update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Maximum sense range
constants.unit: world units, evaluated per AI update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Vertical sense tolerance
constants.unit: world units of height difference, evaluated per AI update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Outer cone angle divisor
constants.unit: divisor applied to pi, giving the radian half-angle at the outer radius, evaluated per AI update in the 60 Hz loop

cards.name: Guard attack sector
cards.summary: Guard attacks use a short reach and a wide forward sector whose authored angle is stored in radians.
cards.behavior: A guard owns an attack reach of 300 world units and a maximum attack half-angle of one third of pi radians. The authored limit is supplied in degrees and converted once with a radians-per-degree factor before it reaches the attack tests. The guard alert table accepts seventeen state indices, and the selector supplies the force state used by the current combat branch.

constants.name: Attack reach
constants.unit: world units, checked per AI update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Attack sector divisor
constants.unit: divisor applied to pi, giving the radian half-angle of the attack sector, held per AI update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Degrees-to-radians factor
constants.unit: radians per degree, applied once when the attack limit is assigned during 60 Hz setup

cards.name: Alarm network fan-out
cards.summary: The alarm is the shared brain for a room of stealth geometry: one trigger can drive many sensors, guards and breakable relays, with fixed upper limits on each list.
cards.behavior: An alarm object stores lists of linked sensors, guards, breakable alarm relays and scripted reaction entries, so a single room-wide trigger can flip every linked sensor and alert every linked guard at once. Linking stops silently once a list reaches its cap, which keeps the fan-out bounded even in heavily populated rooms. A trigger call maps three event kinds onto alarm states, while disabling a breakable relay increments a counter that the alarm can consult before re-arming.

constants.name: Sensor links per alarm
constants.unit: object entries, fixed at level link time with no per-frame growth, in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Guard links per alarm
constants.unit: object entries, fixed at level link time with no per-frame growth, in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Breakable relay links per alarm
constants.unit: object entries, fixed at level link time with no per-frame growth, in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Reaction slots per alarm
constants.unit: scripted mapping entries, fixed at level link time with no per-frame growth, in the 60 Hz loop

cards.name: Laser tripwire sweep and re-arm delay
cards.summary: Laser beams grow and shrink over a requested duration, filter which objects they sense and stay down if an alarm was switched off moments earlier.
cards.behavior: A laser sensor starts with a full normalized draw length. Retracting or extending writes a normalized rate equal to one divided by the requested duration, so the beam reaches its target length in that time and the draw routine integrates the rate each update. Disabling the sensor while its alarm was turned off within the last fifth of a second flags it to remain disabled instead of re-arming on the next cycle. Each sensor also keeps a short filtered list of objects it may or may not trigger.

constants.name: Beam draw maximum
constants.unit: normalized beam length fraction, integrated per 60 Hz update

constants.name: Object trigger slots
constants.unit: object ids per sensor, fixed at level link time with no per-frame growth, in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Retract rate coefficient
constants.unit: beam fraction per second, divided by the requested retract duration and integrated per 60 Hz update

constants.name: Extend rate coefficient
constants.unit: beam fraction per second, divided by the requested extend duration and integrated per 60 Hz update

constants.name: Re-arm suppression window
constants.unit: seconds of game time, compared per sensor update in the 60 Hz loop

cards.name: Coin bounce and collection
cards.summary: Coins pop out with a capped bounce speed, lose energy on each ground contact, glint occasionally and despawn on a short randomized lifetime.
cards.behavior: A coin begins with a bounce radius that decides when it is close enough to the ground to rebound, and a capped initial speed that prevents a huge launch. Horizontal velocity retains sixty percent and vertical velocity retains seventy-five percent per bounce, so a coin settles quickly instead of skittering across the room. It becomes collectible within fifty units, has a one-in-four chance to glint, and disappears after a randomized eight to ten seconds so stray coins do not accumulate.

constants.name: Bounce trigger radius
constants.unit: world units, evaluated per collectible update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Initial bounce speed cap
constants.unit: world units per second, applied once when the coin is launched in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Collect radius
constants.unit: world units, evaluated per player update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Last bounce speed
constants.unit: world units per second, threshold checked per 60 Hz bounce update

constants.name: Horizontal restitution
constants.unit: dimensionless velocity multiplier per bounce at 60 Hz

constants.name: Vertical restitution
constants.unit: dimensionless velocity multiplier per bounce at 60 Hz

constants.name: Glint probability
constants.unit: chance per spawn, rolled once when the coin is created in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Minimum lifetime
constants.unit: seconds of game time, checked per 60 Hz update

constants.name: Maximum lifetime
constants.unit: seconds of game time, checked per 60 Hz update

cards.name: Lucky charm pickup
cards.summary: Charms use a wider pickup radius and lower vertical bounce than coins, then swirl away when collected.
cards.behavior: A lucky charm is tuned to be easier to touch than a coin: both its ground-bounce radius and its collect radius are sixty units. It can be launched faster than a coin but loses half of its vertical speed on each bounce and three quarters of its horizontal speed, so it drops heavily and stops moving sooner. Collecting it starts a swirl state and a collection sound, and it glints about one time in three.

constants.name: Charm bounce radius
constants.unit: world units, evaluated per collectible update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Charm collect radius
constants.unit: world units, evaluated per player update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Charm bounce speed cap
constants.unit: world units per second, applied once when the charm is launched in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Charm horizontal restitution
constants.unit: dimensionless velocity multiplier per bounce at 60 Hz

constants.name: Charm vertical restitution
constants.unit: dimensionless velocity multiplier per bounce at 60 Hz

constants.name: Charm glint probability
constants.unit: chance per spawn, rolled once when the charm is created in the 60 Hz loop

cards.name: Key pickup and persistence
cards.summary: Keys bounce higher and glint far more than other prizes but have a small collect radius, and already-collected keys stay hidden on respawn.
cards.behavior: A key is a small, bright objective item: its bounce and collect radii are only thirty-five units, but it can leave the ground at twice the speed of a coin and it glints three times out of four. Half of its vertical speed survives each bounce while horizontal speed loses forty percent, so it hops noticeably before settling. When a level is loaded after the key was already collected, the key starts in its removed state so it cannot be picked up twice.

constants.name: Key bounce radius
constants.unit: world units, evaluated per collectible update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Key collect radius
constants.unit: world units, evaluated per player update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Key bounce speed cap
constants.unit: world units per second, applied once when the key is launched in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Key last bounce speed
constants.unit: world units per second, threshold checked per 60 Hz bounce update

constants.name: Key horizontal restitution
constants.unit: dimensionless velocity multiplier per bounce at 60 Hz

constants.name: Key vertical restitution
constants.unit: dimensionless velocity multiplier per bounce at 60 Hz

constants.name: Key glint probability
constants.unit: chance per spawn, rolled once when the key is created in the 60 Hz loop

cards.name: Breakable prop shard lifecycle
cards.summary: Breakable scenery records which causes may shatter it, then leaves shard pieces that wait a frame before fading out.
cards.behavior: A breakable keeps a bit mask of what may destroy it. The default breakable accepts player contact and bombs, while the fragile variant accepts only player contact. Breaking it queues shard pieces whose state moves from idle to pending; a pending shard must have been static for more than one rendered frame, or exceed its lifetime, before it switches to fading and starts its per-piece fade. The default coin payout is negative, meaning the object drops no coin unless a level overrides it.

constants.name: Shard pending delay
constants.unit: rendered frames at 60 Hz; a shard must have been static for more than this count before it can fade

constants.name: Default break cause mask
constants.unit: break-cause bit flags (player contact plus bomb), set once when the prop spawns in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Default coin payout
constants.unit: coin count sentinel meaning no payout, set once when the prop spawns in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Fragile break cause mask
constants.unit: break-cause bit flag for player contact only, set once when the fragile prop spawns in the 60 Hz loop

cards.name: Predictive banking into turns
cards.summary: A dedicated animation layer adds a lean to moving objects and looks a quarter second ahead when it computes that lean.
cards.behavior: Banking is a separate animation layer attached to an object. It carries a full-strength lean factor and a prediction interval, and its rotation goal is computed from motion slightly in the future rather than the current frame. As a result a running character or vehicle rolls into a turn before the turn fully develops, which makes fast direction changes read as weight instead of a sudden snap.

constants.name: Bank strength
constants.unit: dimensionless lean multiplier, applied per animation update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Bank prediction interval
constants.unit: seconds of game time ahead, evaluated per animation update in the 60 Hz loop

cards.name: Missile target-lead prediction
cards.summary: Missiles are bombs with trajectory following enabled, and they cap target prediction at half a second so guidance stays believable.
cards.behavior: A missile is built on the bomb base and switches on trajectory following when it spawns. Its guidance may extrapolate a moving target position, but never further than half a second into the future. Bombs themselves arm by storing a detonation time equal to the current game time plus a requested fuse, which gives missile warheads and planted bombs the same timed trigger.

constants.name: Target prediction horizon
constants.unit: seconds of game time, clamped per missile guidance update in the 60 Hz loop

constants.name: Trajectory-following flag
constants.unit: boolean flag, set once when the missile spawns in the 60 Hz loop
